messages.subject: contrast matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am wondering if the order of groups in a contrast matrix matters. To test it, I have generated the two attached ones and passed them through the following lines of code.

contrast_matrix <- as.data.frame(fread('./Data/test1.tsv'))
rownames(contrast_matrix) <- contrast_matrix$Name
contrast_matrix$Name <- NULL
contrast_matrix[is.na <http://is.na>(contrast_matrix)] <- 0
contrast_matrix <- as.matrix(contrast_matrix)

And then tried "groupComparison" on the same dataset using these two  contrast matrices. Do you expect any difference in terms of the results? And this is the order of the groups in the dataset - the same as "test2.tsv".

levels(df.MSstats.proc.Imputed$FeatureLevelData$GROUP)
[1] "D0_RPMI" "D0_RPMI_t1" "D1_BG_r1" "D1_LPS_r1" "D1_LPS_t1" "D1_MDP_r1" "D1_RPMI_r1" "D1_RPMI_t1"
[9] "D1_UA_r1" "D1_UA_t1" "D1_oxLDL_r1" "D1_oxLDL_t1" "D6_BG_r1" "D6_LPS_r1" "D6_MDP_r1" "D6_MDP_t1"
[17] "D6_RPMI_r1" "D6_UA_r1" "D6_oxLDL_r1" "D7_BG_r1" "D7_LPS_r1" "D7_MDP_r1" "D7_RPMI_r1" "D7_UA_r1"
[25] "D7_oxLDL_r1"

What I see is that for the common significantly regulated proteins (2384), the results (logfc and pval) are the same. But " test1.tsv" reults in more regulated proteins (3420) when compared to "test2.tsv" (2539) for all three comparisons combined. How do you explain this?

Best,
Amir

messages.subject: Error in .mergeAnnotation:
messages.body_plain:
Hey there,

Seems to be a common error, but I too am having issues using PDtoMSStatsTMTFormat argument.  The error states:

Error in .mergeAnnotation(input, annotation) :
  ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data.

But the names clearly match.  Here's the complete command and output:

> input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(rawd,
+                                  annotation = anno,
+                                  which.proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions",
+                                  useNumProteinsColumn = FALSE)
I
NFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:43] ** Raw data from ProteomeDiscoverer imported successfully.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:51] ** Raw data from ProteomeDiscoverer cleaned successfully.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:51] ** Using provided annotation.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:51] ** Run and Channel labels were standardized to remove symbols such as '.' or '%'.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:51] ** The following options are used:
  - Features will be defined by the columns: PeptideSequence, PrecursorCharge
  - Shared peptides will be removed.
  - Proteins with single feature will not be removed.
  - Features with less than 3 measurements within each run will be removed.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:52] ** Features with all missing measurements across channels within each run are removed.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:53] ** Shared peptides are removed.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:21:54] ** Features with one or two measurements across channels within each run are removed.
INFO  [2023-01-30 10:22:15] ** PSMs have been aggregated to peptide ions.

Error in .mergeAnnotation(input, annotation) :
  ** Please check the annotation file. The channel name must be matched with that in input data.

I've tried different options for the `which.proteinid` and `useNumProteinsColumn` arguments to no avail.

Attached is an excel workbook with top 5 rows for the PSM output from PD, the annotation file.

Kind regards,
Anasta
